title: A. Good Pairs
statement:
You are given an array a_1, a_2, …, a_n of positive integers. A good pair is a pair of indices (i, j) with 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n such that, for all 1 ≤ k ≤ n, the following equality holds:

|a_i - a_k| + |a_k - a_j| = |a_i - a_j|, where |x| denotes the absolute value of x.

Find a good pair. Note that i can be equal to j.

The input consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) — the number of test cases. Description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) — the length of the array.

The second line of each test case contains n integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^9) where a_i is the i-th element of the array.

The sum of n for all test cases is at most 2·10^5.

For each test case, print a single line with two space-separated indices i and j which form a good pair of the array. The case i=j is allowed. It can be shown that such a pair always exists. If there are multiple good pairs, print any of them.

In the first case, for i = 2 and j = 3 the equality holds true for all k:

Input:
```
335 2 751 4 2 2 312
```

Output:
```
2 3
1 2
1 1
```
